Primary request: S3 — Checkpoint Lanes.
Scene and subject: Tense municipal checkpoint streets: narrow crooked approaches open into a clear inspection court framed by a stone guard loggia, converted civic office, compact medieval guardhouse and iron gate piers. Barricade groups sit along edges with an obvious passable dogleg route. A few shielded inspection lamps and one organized overhead service gantry add early industrial control. Security architecture is visibly different from ordinary courtyard homes while belonging to the same city.
Composition specific to this plate: a crooked street expands into an offset municipal inspection court, then leaves through a deliberate open iron checkpoint. Stone guard loggia and compact slate-roof gatehouse with thick piers establish a security silhouette; converted office is offset behind the perimeter. Keep the broad visible dogleg passage between perimeter barricade groups obviously open. Invent this street arrangement, rather than duplicating the reference's central portico facade. Keep ground texture subdued enough to read the dogleg at a glance.
Color palette and lighting: cool gray limestone, slate, aged iron, subdued green-gray banners and selective warm lamps; readable overcast daylight.
Deliverable filename: 03-s3-checkpoint-lanes.png; do not render the filename in the picture.
Targeted retry corrections: Show ZERO people anywhere; the architectural doorway proportions establish human scale. This must be readable OVERCAST daylight with soft shadows, quieter broad gray ground planes and fewer individual high-contrast paving marks. Preserve the checkpoint identity, open dogleg route, north-up steep roof/south-facade camera and approved material language. Create the final selected independent environment plate.
images.qa: Viewed both originals. Selected retry improves softer daylight, broad ground grouping and clearly bent open inspection route; guard loggia, open iron gate, compact guardhouse, banners and edge barricades establish checkpoint identity. Zero figures, no HUD/text. Residual uniform roof/paving line contrast remains; overhead gantry from the first version is absent in selected plate, but organized services and gate control retain theme identity.

Primary request: S4 — Collapsed Ward.
Scene and subject: A damaged inhabited ward with one partially collapsed masonry hall, roofless arched shells, a surviving slate-roof tenement and a breached courtyard wall. Collapse follows believable structural bays; rubble collects at the failed footprints and sparse weeds reclaim edges. An irregular connected street snakes through the district and the combat center remains clear. Show cut stone, fragments of muted clay roof and old civic infrastructure, not a desert ruin or a sea of rubble.
Composition specific to this plate: create a visibly damaged ward, with the broken hall and exposed arched bays defining an irregular side of a clear winding street. A surviving inhabited slate-roof tenement anchors a different edge. Keep collapse debris within the failed building footprints and wall edges, with a generous quiet irregular combat pocket connected through the whole scene. Invent the arrangement, not the reference's intact central portico.
Important art direction refinement: reference supplies camera/material identity; use noticeably SIMPLER PAINTERLY VALUE GROUPS. VERY QUIET large ground planes with soft broad color patches; paving divisions barely suggested in low contrast, disappearing into distance and shadow. Roofs read as broad slate/clay masses with a few grouped tile indications, not uniform dark tile grid lines. Fewer tiny service accents and piping; broad eave/contact shadows describe volume. Avoid sharp equal-strength mortar outlines and repeated noisy texture. Broken structure has selective crisp focal edges against quieter ground, not detail everywhere.
Color palette and lighting: gray limestone, subdued dusty clay, temperate scrub and soft fresh greens; pale sun and soft shadow.
Deliverable filename: 04-s4-collapsed-ward.png; do not render the filename in the picture.
images.qa: Viewed generated original. Correct north-up camera and coherent city materials. Partially collapsed arched hall, bay-aligned broken roof and concentrated footprint rubble contrast with surviving slate tenement. Winding connected street stays clear, vegetation is temperate, one scale figure, no HUD/text. Roof and ground value groups improved somewhat, but residual over-lined paving, tiles and facade detail remains; not a claim that noise is fully solved.

Primary request: S5 — Inner District Gate.
Scene and subject: A major inner-city gate as a mid-city milestone: two substantial gatehouse masses set into a Roman/medieval defensive wall, one clear arched passage, flanking inspection offices and a compact industrial winch house. A broad empty encounter court dominates the foreground with routes running around its perimeter. Restrained civic heraldic cloth, aged iron gate machinery and heavy deep stone returns convey authority. Avoid filling the encounter court with statues or crates.
Composition specific to this plate: substantial twin gatehouse blocks and a single deep clear arched passage anchor the continuous thick inner-city wall. Inspection offices and one compact winch house are subordinate. A very broad almost empty irregular foreground encounter court frames the gate; organic perimeter routes connect into it. Clear mid-city gate milestone, visibly distinct from the smaller checkpoint and from a civic admissions facade. Fewer tiny service ornaments, gate machinery follows the actual wall and winch structure.
CRITICAL PAINTING PRIORITY: noticeably quiet broad value planes. Treat the reference as CAMERA AND MATERIAL language, not as a texture-density target. Paint a broad soft gray limestone court with only a handful of faint paving joint suggestions; DO NOT draw a dark grid around each stone. Roof surfaces are large calm slate color masses with sparse grouped hints of tile courses, DO NOT delineate every tile. Broad eave/contact shadows and major wall returns give convincing light and depth. Keep focal sharp edges at the deep gate arch and organized iron/bronze mechanism. No repeated tiny pipe details, no uniformly noisy masonry texture. Surface simplicity must leave the empty encounter ground readable immediately.
Color palette and lighting: pale cool stone, dark slate, aged bronze and muted plum-gray cloth; bright cloud-filtered daylight.
